summary: Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She was a graduate student at McMaster University, where she studied under Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the Catholic University of America under the supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli works in philosophy and other fields. He earned his PhD from École Polytechnique under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.
Diego Loukota specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Heidelberg under Hermann Berger, held academic posts there, and served as Director of the Institute for Indology and Tamilistics at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indologist. He succeeded Wolfgang Voigt and held a post at the Prussian State Library from around 1972 to 1985.

Dieter Schlingloff is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Göttingen and Berlin, he taught at Kiel University (1968–1971) and served as Honorary Professor at the University of Munich (1972–1996) and Leipzig (2005).

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he later served as professor (1978–2007). He founded and served as Managing Director of the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and Indologist. After completing his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania, he held the Chair of the History of South Asia at the University of Heidelberg from 1968 to 2001.

Dilgo Khyentse (1910–1991) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, taught numerous students, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at the universities of Calcutta and Delhi before serving as Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, later holding posts at Visva-Bharati University and the University of Calcutta.
Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras, a D.Litt. from Patna University, and taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University (circa 1999–2002) and Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2002–2017).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was a Danish Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and later served there as a professor from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and was Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Anagarika Munindra, and taught students including Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, and Sylvia Boorstein.
Dipak Kumar Barua is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer and faculty dean at the University of Calcutta and became head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara around 1996.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held posts at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).
